devices.name: Metonymy
devices.definition: Naming something by a word closely associated with it — cause for effect, container for contents, author for writings.

occurrences.note: Who subvert whole houses: i.e., families
A prophet of their own. Epiminedes was not a prophet except in the opinion of the Cretans. See under Gnome
That they may be sound in the faith: i.e., the doctrine of the Gospel. Jude 3. Earnestly contend for the faith: i.e., the true doctrine of Christ
Looking for that blessed hope: i.e., that blessed object of hope, the coming of Christ. 4. LOVE is put for the person or object loved

devices.name: Synonymia
devices.definition: Amassing synonyms — words of like meaning — to enforce and enlarge a point.

occurrences.note: In all the other epistles it is only grace, or grace and peace. In these three epistles mercy is added: as though to imply that with the many responsibilities of the pastoral office, Gods mercy would

devices.name: Idiom
devices.definition: A peculiar usage of the Hebrew or Greek that does not carry its literal force — an idiom to be rendered by its sense, not word for word.

occurrences.note: where it is used as an adjective, and in its ordinary sense of malicious accuser. ( diatheekee ). In classical Greek it had two meanings: (1) a last will or testament, and (2) very rarely, of a cove

devices.name: Enallage
devices.definition: Exchange of one grammatical part or form for another, differing from strict usage for effect.

occurrences.note: The appearing of the glory of our great God and Saviour: i.e., the glorious appearing of the great God, even our Saviour Jesus Christ

devices.name: Heterosis
devices.definition: Exchange of one grammatical form for another — of tense, number, person, degree, or mood (e.g. a future used for a command).

devices.name: Synecdoche
devices.definition: Substituting a part for the whole, or the whole for a part (“all the world”; “flesh and blood”).

occurrences.note: Slow bellies: i.e., slow persons, who by reason of large eating, have grown stout and move slowly. 19. The WOMB is put for a female, in respect to her being marriageable Judges 5:30. A wombtwo wombs

devices.name: Hendiadys
devices.definition: One idea expressed by two words joined with “and,” the second really qualifying the first.

occurrences.note: Looking for that blessed hope and the glorious appearing. Not two things but one: our hope is the glorious appearing! The latter clause is also Hendiadys: One Person being meant, not two: the appear

devices.name: Hyperbaton
devices.definition: Words wrenched out of their natural order, throwing weight onto the displaced word.

occurrences.note: Faithful the saying. How much more emphatic than the ordinary coldness of the natural order: The saying is faithful

devices.name: Paroemia (proverb)
devices.definition: A proverb — a wayside-saying in common use, cited or coined.

devices.name: Gnome (quotation)
devices.definition: A quotation or proverbial maxim woven in — a pithy saying cited for authority or point.

occurrences.note: One of themselves, even a prophet of their own, said, The Cretians are alway liars, evil beasts, slow bellies (i.e., liars, evil wild-beasts, gluttons, lazy). This involves another figure called Oxym

devices.name: Amphibologia
devices.definition: A saying deliberately capable of two meanings, both intended.

devices.name: Anthropopatheia
devices.definition: Ascribing to God human feelings, parts, or actions, by way of condescension to us.

devices.name: Palinodia
devices.definition: A concession — granting a point for argument's sake before answering it.

occurrences.note: Zealous of good works: i.e., with respect to good works
